This is non-negotiable. Playable canon characters wreck internal hierarchy instantly, because nobody outranks Anakin Skywalker.

docs.title: 5. Jedi Policy
docs.text:
Jedi are the most-abused role in every SWRP community. The policy here is deliberately restrictive.

  • Hard cap: 8% of the active roster, rounded down, with an absolute ceiling of 10 slots.
  • Application-only. Written application plus interview with the Jedi Council roles. No tryouts, no first-come.
  • Ranks: Youngling (probationary) → Padawan → Knight → Master → Council Member. Council is capped at 3.
  • No Jedi Generals at launch. The GAR command structure runs the war. A Jedi General is a campaign unlock, not a starting position.
  • Mechanically support-oriented. Force abilities on this server emphasize saber defense, deflection, push/pull, and battlefield utility. Jedi are durable and useful, not one-man armies. Damage output is deliberately modest.
  • Force powers permitted: saber combat and deflection, Force push/pull, Force jump, Force speed (brief), Force sense, mind trick (on NPCs only, never on player characters), Force healing (self, slow).
  • Force powers not permitted: lightning, choke, drain, precognitive combat awareness that overrides other players' actions, and any power that removes another player's control of their character.
  • Chain of command: Jedi advise; they do not command GAR units outside of specifically assigned operations. A Jedi Knight cannot order a Sergeant to do their laundry.

docs.title: 6.1 Armor
docs.text:
Phase II is standard issue. Phase I appears only on long-service veterans as a personal choice, and requires a rank of Sergeant or above plus a written justification. Mixed Phase I/II kit is permitted for veterans.

Permitted attachments: kama, pauldron, macrobinoculars, rangefinder (specialist roles), antenna (comms), visor tint variation, unit markings, personal markings.

Not permitted: Mandalorian armor, jetpacks outside of specific qualified roles, ARC trooper kit without ARC qualification, Commando armor (locked unit), and any armor from outside the era.

docs.title: 6.2 Weapons
docs.text:
Standard armory: DC-15A blaster rifle, DC-15S carbine, DC-17 pistol, DC-15x sniper (Marksman qual), Z-6 rotary cannon (Heavy Weapons qual), RPS-6 launcher (Heavy Weapons qual), thermal detonators (EOD or Assault role), vibroblade.

Dual DC-17s are ARC-only. Lightsabers are Jedi-only. Anything not on the armory list requires a Lore Officer ruling.

docs.title: 6.3 Vehicles
docs.text: LAAT/i gunship, ARC-170, V-19 Torrent, BARC speeder, AT-RT, AT-TE, Venator-class Star Destroyer (home station). All flight and armor operation is qualification-gated.

docs.title: 6.4 Enemy Forces
docs.text:
Separatist Droid Army: B1 battle droids, B2 super battle droids, droidekas, BX commando droids, tactical droids, dwarf spider droids, AATs, vulture droids, Trade Federation and Techno Union assets.

Secondary antagonists available to event planners: pirates, mercenaries, planetary insurgents, rogue Republic elements.

docs.title: 7. Home Station
docs.text:
RSD [SHIP NAME], a Venator-class Star Destroyer. Republic Star Destroyer designation.

Assumed complement: our roster represents a detachment, not the ship's full crew of thousands. Unnamed background personnel are assumed present and are not roleplayed.

Standard compartments: bridge, hangar deck, armory, medbay, barracks (by battalion), brig, briefing room, simulation deck, engineering, mess.

Access control by rank and qualification — the bridge is not a hangout, and the armory is not self-serve.

docs.title: 8. Deviations Register
docs.text:
Deliberate departures from source material, with reasoning. This section is the honest list. Anyone who catches us contradicting canon should find it here.

Deviation Reasoning Original Outer Rim campaign theater Narrative freedom without contradicting canon events No named canon characters playable Prevents unbeatable in-character authority Jedi capped and support-oriented Balance and roleplay integrity No Jedi General at launch Preserves GAR chain of command as the primary structure Legends-permissive sourcing More material to draw from; better roleplay Compressed unit structure (5 battalions) A half-empty battalion is worse than no battalion Order 66 does not occur Server continuity Simulation deck used for instanced content Lore-plausible extension of canon clone training Qualification system Original mechanic; loosely inspired by real military MOS/quals

docs.title: 9. Ruling Process
docs.text:
When something isn't covered here:

  1. Ask in the lore channel. Most questions are answered in a minute by someone who knows.
  2. If unresolved, file a Ruling Request — a short post stating the question, the sources you've found, and what you'd like to do.
  3. The Lore Officer rules within 7 days. Rulings are published in the rulings log.
  4. Rulings are binding and become part of this document at the next revision.
  5. Management may overturn a Lore Officer ruling, in writing, with reasoning published.

Standing guidance for rulings: when in doubt, favor the option that produces better roleplay for more players over the option that is more technically accurate. We are running a community, not a citation exercise.

docs.title: 10. The Attitude We Want
docs.text:
Lore knowledge is a way to make the world feel real. It is not a status game.

  • Correct people kindly and once. "Hey, we're Phase II standard here — Phase I needs Sergeant and a write-up" is helpful. Six paragraphs with wiki links is not.
  • Do not lore-lawyer during operations. If something's wrong, note it and raise it after.
  • New players get latitude. Someone who thinks all clones are named Rex is a person we haven't taught yet.
  • The Lore Officer's job is to enable, not to gatekeep. If someone has a cool idea that bends the setting slightly, the default answer is "let's find a way."

Canon Scope v1.0 — Effective [DATE] — Rulings log maintained separately

docs.title: [SERVER NAME] — Grand Army of the Republic Military Roleplay
docs.text: Document 1 of 6 · Version 1.0 · Authority: Management

docs.title: Article I — Purpose
docs.text:
[SERVER NAME] exists to recreate the experience of belonging to a military unit — structure, shared routine, earned responsibility, and small-unit cohesion — inside the Star Wars universe on Garry's Mod.

We are not a deathmatch server with rank tags, and we are not a punishment simulator. We are a community where the chain of command is load-bearing, where what you can do is something you earned, and where the people next to you are the reason you log in.

Three commitments this community makes to every member:

  1. Rank is earned, never sold. No amount of money moves you up the chain.
  2. Authority is accountable. Every punishment has evidence, every decision has an appeal, and no one is above the process — including the owner.
  3. Effort is recognized. Time you put in is logged, visible, and counts toward something.

docs.title: Article II — Scope and Jurisdiction
docs.text:
This Charter governs conduct in all [SERVER NAME] spaces:

  • The Garry's Mod game server(s), including staging and event servers
  • The official Discord server, including voice channels and DMs between members regarding server business
  • The community website, forums, and personnel records system
  • Steam group, Workshop collection comments, and any official social accounts

Off-platform conduct is generally outside our jurisdiction, with three exceptions where we will act regardless of where it occurred: 1. Credible threats of violence against a member 2. Sexual misconduct involving a minor 3. Coordinated harassment or doxxing of a member

Age policy: Minimum age 15. Members under 18 are not eligible for Management or Head of Staff positions.

docs.title: Article III — Core Rules
docs.text: Rules are grouped by category. The number in brackets is the enforcement tier (see Article IV).

docs.title: Section 1 — Conduct
docs.text: # Rule Tier 1.1 Treat every member with basic respect. Banter is welcome; targeted cruelty is not. 1 1.2 No slurs or hate speech of any kind, in any context, including "as a joke" or "in character." 3 1.3 No harassment, stalking, or repeated unwanted contact after being asked to stop. 3 1.4 No sexual content, sexual roleplay, or sexualized discussion. This is a military RP server. 3 1.5 No doxxing. Do not share anyone's real name, location, workplace, images, or contact info without their explicit permission. 4 1.6 No discussion of real-world politics, religion, or active conflicts in public channels. 1 1.7 Do not misrepresent yourself as staff, command, or a Lucasfilm/Disney representative. 2 1.8 Do not encourage, glorify, or instruct on self-harm. If a member appears to be in crisis, notify staff privately rather than engaging publicly. 3 1.9 Do not advertise other servers or communities without Management approval. 2 1.10 Do not bring drama from other communities here. 1

docs.title: Section 2 — Roleplay
docs.text: # Rule Tier 2.1 Stay in character during formations, operations, and training. Out-of-character talk in these contexts requires the prefix // or use of OOC chat. 1 2.2 No metagaming — do not use out-of-character information (Discord, spectator view, a friend's stream) to inform in-character decisions. 2 2.3 No powergaming — do not force outcomes on other players' characters or narrate their actions for them. 2 2.4 No fail-RP — act consistently with your character's rank, training, and situation. A CT does not order a Colonel around. 1 2.5 Respect the chain of command in character. Disagreements go up the chain, not sideways into an argument. 1 2.6 No random deathmatch. Violence against friendly players requires in-character justification and, above a scuffle, a staff-approved scenario. 3 2.7 Follow the New Life Rule: on death, your character does not remember the events immediately preceding it and does not return to that engagement for 10 minutes. 2 2.8 Do not break an active event or operation. If you have a problem, report it after or use a staff sit. 2 2.9 Jedi may not use the Force to resolve out-of-character disputes or to bypass established procedure. 1

docs.title: Section 3 — Gameplay and Technical
docs.text: # Rule Tier 3.1 No exploiting bugs, glitches, or unintended mechanics. Report them instead — reporting is rewarded. 3 3.2 No cheating, scripts, macros, aim assistance, wallhacks, or third-party clients. 5 3.3 No prop abuse — no prop killing, prop blocking, prop climbing to out-of-bounds areas, or prop spam. 2 3.4 Do not enter out-of-bounds or non-playable map areas. 2 3.5 Do not intentionally crash, lag, or disrupt the server. 5 3.6 Do not evade a ban with an alternate account. 5 3.7 Do not share or sell your account. You are responsible for everything done on it. 4 3.8 Do not AFK at your post for extended periods to farm duty credits. Log off instead. 1

docs.title: Section 4 — Communications
docs.text: # Rule Tier 4.1 No microphone spam, earrape, soundboards, or music over voice comms. 2 4.2 Keep radio nets clear during operations. Brevity is a discipline, not a suggestion. (See SOP §3) 1 4.3 Do not speak over command during a formation or briefing. 1 4.4 Push-to-talk is required. Open mic is not permitted on operation nets. 1 4.5 English on primary comms so leadership can maintain situational awareness. Other languages welcome in social channels and squad-private comms. 1

docs.title: Section 5 — Staff and Command Interaction
docs.text: # Rule Tier 5.1 Comply with staff instructions during a sit. Argue the case, not the person. Appeal afterward if you disagree. 2 5.2 Do not disconnect to avoid a staff sit. 3 5.3 Do not file knowingly false reports against another member. 3 5.4 Do not "staff shop" — asking a second staff member to overturn a first one's ruling. Use the appeals process. 2 5.5 Do not pressure, guilt, or bribe staff or command for rank, quals, or leniency. 2

docs.title: Tier Definitions
docs.text: Tier Nature First Offense Second Third 1 Minor / correctable Verbal warning (logged) Formal warning 1–3 day ban 2 Disruptive Formal warning 1–3 day ban 7 day ban 3 Serious 3–7 day ban 14–30 day ban Permanent 4 Severe 30 day ban Permanent — 5 Zero tolerance Permanent — —

docs.title: Governing Principles
docs.text:
Correction before punishment. Tier 1 violations from a new member get an explanation first. A rule nobody explained to them is a rule we failed to teach, not a rule they broke.

Warnings expire. Tier 1 and 2 warnings drop off your record after 90 days of clean conduct. Tier 3+ records are permanent but are considered in context.

Staff may adjust one tier in either direction with written justification in the log. Adjustments of more than one tier require Senior Administrator approval.

Aggravating factors (may raise a tier): premeditation, targeting a new member, abuse of a leadership or staff position, repeating the same offense after correction, doing it during a public event.

Mitigating factors (may lower a tier): self-reporting, genuine confusion about the rule, immediate cessation on being asked, clean record over long tenure.

Punishments run parallel, not stacked. A single incident produces one punishment, not one per rule technically broken.

docs.title: Non-Ban Sanctions
docs.text:
Available where a ban is disproportionate:

Sanction Use case Voice mute (1–72h) Comms violations Text mute (1–72h) Chat violations Prop restriction Prop abuse Job/battalion restriction Persistent fail-RP in a specific role Qualification suspension Negligence with a qualified capability (see Command Handbook §6) Command probation Leadership failure, IC misconduct by an officer

docs.title: The Right of Appeal
docs.text: Every punishment is appealable. No exceptions, including permanent bans and including punishments issued by Management.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. File — Submit an appeal via the appeals form on the website or Discord. Appeals require: your Steam ID, the punishment, the issuing staff member, and your account of what happened.
  2. Assignment — The appeal is assigned to a staff member who was not involved in the original punishment and who is at least equal in rank to the issuer.
  3. Review — The reviewer examines the attached evidence, the logs, and both accounts. They may request additional statements.
  4. Ruling — Uphold, reduce, or overturn. Ruling is delivered in writing with reasoning.
  5. Escalation — A denied appeal may be escalated once to the Head of Staff, or to the Ombudsman if the Head of Staff was involved.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Response SLA: 72 hours. An appeal with no response in 72 hours is automatically escalated to the Head of Staff.
  • Evidence burden is on the server, not the accused. If a punishment has no evidence attached to the log, the appeal is granted automatically. This rule is absolute and has no exceptions.
  • Appeals are not popularity contests. Community sentiment, Discord petitions, and "everyone likes them" are not evidence and carry no weight.
  • Cooling-off period: one appeal per punishment. A second appeal on the same punishment may be filed after 30 days if new evidence exists.
  • Bad-faith appeals (abusive, spam, obviously fabricated) may be closed without review and count as a Tier 1 offense.

docs.title: The Ombudsman
docs.text:
One community member, appointed by Management for a 6-month term, who: - Is not in the staff or command chain - Can receive any complaint, including about Management - Has standing to escalate directly to the Owner - Publishes a quarterly summary of complaint volume and categories (anonymized)

This role exists so that grievances have somewhere to go other than a Discord blowup.

docs.title: Article VI — Data and Privacy
docs.text:
• We log gameplay actions, chat, punishments, and duty time. Logs are retained 12 months.
  • Voice is not recorded by default. Members may record their own comms for evidence; recording others is permitted only for evidence purposes and may not be published outside a report.
  • We do not collect real-world personal information. Do not provide it to staff, and staff must not request it.
  • Members may request deletion of their personnel record on departure. Punishment records are retained regardless, as they are the basis of ban enforcement.

docs.title: Article VII — Monetization Policy
docs.text:
What may be purchased: cosmetic customization, callsign slots, extra character slots, queue priority, and quality-of-life conveniences.

What may never be purchased, under any circumstance: rank, battalion membership, qualifications, staff positions, command positions, combat advantage, immunity from rules, or leniency in punishment.

All payments are donations toward server operating costs. Nothing sold is a Star Wars product; this is a non-commercial fan community and holds no license from Lucasfilm or Disney.

Donations do not create standing in any dispute. A donor and a non-donor receive identical treatment in a sit, an appeal, and a promotion board. Staff who give preferential treatment to donors face Tier 3 sanction.

docs.title: Article VIII — Amendment
docs.text:
• Amendments are proposed by any member via the suggestions channel, or by Management directly.
  • Amendments require Management approval and a 7-day notice period before taking effect, except for emergency amendments addressing an active exploit or safety issue, which take effect immediately and are reviewed within 7 days.
  • All amendments are logged in a public changelog with date and reasoning.
  • Rules are not retroactive. You cannot be punished for conduct that was permitted at the time.

docs.title: Article IX — Acknowledgment
docs.text:
Membership in [SERVER NAME] constitutes acceptance of this Charter. Ignorance of a published rule is a mitigating factor, not a defense.

This Charter is the highest authority in the community. Where any other document conflicts with it, this document governs.

Charter v1.0 — Effective [DATE] — Next scheduled review: [DATE + 6 months]

docs.title: [SERVER NAME] — In-Character Authority
docs.text: Document 5 of 6 · Version 1.0 · Authority: High Command + Management

docs.title: 0. What Command Is
docs.text:
Command is a job, not a prize.

The rank on your shoulder means you are responsible for people. Not that you have earned deference, not that you get better gear, not that you win arguments. Responsible for people — their training, their progression, their experience of this community, and whether they log in next week.

The measure of a good officer on this server is not how well they perform in an operation. It is whether their people are still here in six months and whether one of them is ready to take their job.

docs.title: 1. The Firewall (Restated)
docs.text:
Command rank grants zero staff powers. Staff rank grants zero command authority.

  • A Marshal Commander cannot ban, kick, mute, or warn anyone. Ever.
  • Rule violations get reported to staff. You do not handle them in character.
  • If a trooper cheats, you don't demote them — you report it. If a trooper is a poor squad leader, you don't ban them — you counsel them.
  • Command discipline is for in-character performance. Staff discipline is for rule violations. Do not blur these.

Where they overlap: a trooper who repeatedly RDMs during operations is both a rule violation (staff) and a performance issue (command). Report it to staff and counsel them. Two tracks, both run.

docs.title: 2. The Founder Rule
docs.text:
No member of Management plays a character above the rank of Warrant Officer.

This is a structural rule and it is not waivable.

The moment the owner also sits at the top of the in-character chain, three things happen immediately and irreversibly: every IC decision becomes unappealable, subordinates stop giving honest feedback, and the server becomes one person's story rather than a shared one.

Management plays sergeants, medics, and pilots. That is not a sacrifice — it is where the good roleplay actually is.

docs.title: 3.1 Enlisted
docs.text: Rank Abbrev Role Time in Grade Requirements Clone Trooper CT Recruit — Complete boot camp Trooper Specialist CT-S Qualified trooper 10 hrs Basic Rifleman + 1 additional qual Corporal CPL Fire team 2IC 20 hrs 3 quals, sponsor recommendation Sergeant SGT Fire team leader 40 hrs 4 quals, board, leads a fire team Staff Sergeant SSGT Squad leader 70 hrs 5 quals incl. Instructor, board Warrant Officer WO Technical specialist 100 hrs Deep specialization, board

docs.title: 3.2 Commissioned
docs.text:
Rank Abbrev Role Time in Grade Requirements Second Lieutenant 2LT Platoon leader 100 hrs Board + Officer Course First Lieutenant 1LT Senior platoon leader 140 hrs Board, demonstrated leadership Captain CPT Company commander 200 hrs Board, has trained a subordinate to SGT Major MAJ Battalion executive officer 280 hrs Board, High Command endorsement Lieutenant Colonel LTC Battalion 2IC 360 hrs Board, High Command endorsement Colonel COL Battalion commander 450 hrs Appointment by High Command Commander CMDR Multi-battalion command — Appointment, term-limited Marshal Commander MCMDR GAR ground forces — Appointment, term-limited

Time in Grade is a floor, not an entitlement. Meeting the hours does not create a right to promotion. Nobody is owed a rank for showing up.

docs.title: 3.3 Rank Caps
docs.text:
Ranks are capped by roster size to prevent rank inflation — the disease that turns a server into forty officers commanding six privates.

Roster size Max COL Max MAJ/LTC Max CPT Max officers total Under 30 1 per battalion 1 2 15% of roster 30–60 1 per battalion 2 4 15% of roster 60+ 1 per battalion 3 6 15% of roster

When a rank is capped, promotion requires a vacancy. This is a feature. Scarcity is what makes rank mean something.

docs.title: 4.1 When a Board Is Required
docs.text: All promotions to Sergeant and above. Below Sergeant, a battalion commander may promote directly on meeting the criteria.

docs.title: 4.2 Composition
docs.text:
Promoting to Board composition SGT / SSGT 3 members: 1 officer (chair), 1 SSGT+, 1 NCO from another battalion WO / 2LT / 1LT 3 members: 1 field grade officer (chair), 2 officers, at least 1 external CPT and above 5 members: 1 High Command (chair), 3 officers, 1 external

"External" means from a different battalion than the candidate. At least one external member on every board. This is what prevents battalions becoming closed loops that promote their own regardless of quality.

Recusal: any board member with a close personal relationship to the candidate recuses. Same standard as staff.

docs.title: 4.3 Process
docs.text:
1. Nomination — by the candidate's direct superior, or self-nomination with a sponsoring NCO/officer
  2. Packet submission — personnel file: hours, quals, sponsor statement, any counseling records
  3. Board convenes — scheduled, candidate present, 20–30 minutes
  4. Examination — see §4.4
  5. Deliberation — candidate steps out
  6. Ruling — Promote / Defer with development plan / Deny with reasons
  7. Written feedback to the candidate within 48 hours, always, including on a pass

docs.title: 4.4 Board Content
docs.text:
Area Weight Examples Knowledge 25% SOP, comms procedure, ROE, chain of command, unit lore Leadership 35% Situational judgment: "Your squad lead goes down mid-objective. Walk me through the next 60 seconds." Record 20% Duty hours, op participation, quals, counseling history Peer standing 20% Input from peers and subordinates, solicited privately

Peer and subordinate input is mandatory and weighted. An officer who is beloved by the board and dreaded by their troopers is exactly the officer we must not promote. Ask the people they lead.

docs.title: 4.5 Deferral
docs.text:
Deferral is the default for a candidate who is close but not ready. A deferral must come with: - Specific, written development items - A named mentor - A re-board date (typically 30 days)

Deferral is not a failure. Frame it that way explicitly, out loud, in the room.

docs.title: 5.1 Standards
docs.text: Requirement Standard Duration 30 minutes maximum Notice Announced at least 24 hours in advance Minimum attendees 1 (never cancel on a single candidate — that person made time) Host SGT or above with Instructor qualification Grading Published rubric, scored, shown to the candidate Result Delivered same session, in writing

docs.title: 5.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. Publish the rubric before the tryout. Candidates should know exactly what's being measured.
  2. No hazing. None. Not "tradition," not "building character," not "how it was done for me." Any hazing is an immediate command discipline matter and likely a Charter violation.
  3. No endurance filtering. Making people stand at attention for 40 minutes measures patience, not aptitude, and it selects for the wrong people.
  4. Failure gets specific feedback and a retry date, never a vague "not ready."
  5. Retry cooldown: 7 days. No lifetime bars from a unit.
  6. Cancelled tryouts must be re-announced within 7 days. Repeated cancellation is a leadership failure.

docs.title: 5.3 Standard Tryout Structure
docs.text: Phase Time Measures Formation & bearing 5 min Discipline, presence Knowledge check 5 min SOP, comms, ROE Marksmanship 5 min Range score Practical scenario 10 min Judgment, comms, teamwork Interview 5 min Motivation, fit, availability

docs.title: 6.1 Scope
docs.text:
Command discipline addresses performance and conduct in character: dereliction of a post, insubordination, negligence with a qualified capability, repeated tardiness, failure of leadership responsibility.

It does not address rule violations. Those go to staff. Always.

docs.title: 6.2 Progressive Ladder
docs.text: Step Action Record 1 Verbal counseling — private, corrective conversation Noted in file 2 Written counseling — documented, signed by both, includes a specific improvement plan In file, 90 days 3 Extra duty — additional watch rotations, max 3 sessions In file, 90 days 4 Qualification suspension — pull a qual after negligence; requires recertification In file, until recert 5 Reduction in rank — one grade, requires a board, appealable Permanent record 6 Removal from unit — transfer to another battalion or to unassigned; requires High Command Permanent record

docs.title: 6.3 Rules of Discipline
docs.text:
1. Praise publicly, correct privately. Always. No exceptions.
  2. No mass punishment. Punishing a squad for one person's mistake builds resentment and drives people off the server. It is banned.
  3. No punishment while angry. Wait a session.
  4. Counseling requires a fix. Every counseling names a specific behavior and a specific improvement. "Do better" is not counseling.
  5. Reduction in rank requires a board, and the trooper may bring an advocate.
  6. All command discipline is appealable to the next level of command, and to the Ombudsman if the chain itself is the problem.
  7. Records expire. Verbal and written counseling drop off after 90 days of clean performance.

docs.title: 6.4 Insubordination
docs.text:
Refusing a lawful order in character is a disciplinary matter. But three things are never insubordination:

  • Refusing an order that violates the Charter
  • Asking a clarifying question
  • Raising a concern before executing ("Sir, recommend we approach from the east instead — request permission to advise")

Train your people to speak up. An officer who punishes dissent will be surrounded by silence, and silence is how operations fail.

docs.title: 7.1 Weekly Minimums
docs.text:
Every battalion commander is responsible for:

  • One training session per week, hosted or delegated
  • Roster maintenance — activity check, LOA processing, removals
  • Promotion pipeline — at least one candidate developed toward a board
  • One operation contribution per month — write or lead
  • Presence — minimum 8 hours/week on the server

docs.title: 7.2 Roster Management
docs.text:
Status Definition Action Active 3+ hours in the last 14 days — Low activity Under 3 hours in 14 days Check-in message Inactive Under 1 hour in 21 days, no LOA Removal notice, 7 days to respond LOA Declared absence Held indefinitely, up to 60 days Retired Voluntary departure Rank held for 30 days on return

LOA is free, unlimited, and requires no reason. Post it and go. People have jobs, school, deployments, and lives. A community that punishes absence loses the people worth keeping.

docs.title: 7.3 Succession
docs.text:
Every command position must have a designated and trained second.

If you are a battalion commander and you disappeared tomorrow, your unit should function. If it wouldn't, that is your failure to fix, this week.

  • Designate a 2IC on assuming command
  • 2IC runs at least one training session and one operation per month
  • Handover on departure includes a written brief: roster state, ongoing issues, promotion pipeline, unit traditions

docs.title: 8. Command Term Limits
docs.text:
Position Term Renewal Battalion Commander (COL) 4 months Renewable once, then 2-month step-down Commander (CMDR) 4 months Renewable once Marshal Commander 4 months Renewable once Jedi Council 6 months Renewable once

Why: term limits give leaders a graceful exit that isn't quitting in frustration, they force succession planning to be real, and they prevent the ossification that turns leadership into a permanent clique.

Stepping down at term end carries no stigma. Former commanders retain their rank and typically move into instructor or advisory roles, which are genuinely valuable and much less exhausting.

docs.title: 9. Awards and Recognition
docs.text:
Recognition is free and it is the most underused retention tool available.

Award Criteria Commendation Outstanding performance in a single operation Instructor Ribbon 10 successful certifications delivered Campaign Ribbon Participation in a completed campaign phase Wound Marker Serious casualty sustained in an operation Sponsor Ribbon 5 sponsored recruits reaching Specialist Unit Citation Battalion-level exceptional performance Meritorious Service Sustained contribution over 6 months

Awards appear on the personnel file and as armor markings. Present them in formation, out loud, with a specific reason. "For pulling two casualties out under fire at Sullust" beats a Discord ping every time.

Recognize the unglamorous. The person who ran the armory post reliably for three months deserves more recognition than the one who got a lucky kill in an op. Design your award practice around that.

docs.title: 10. The Officer's Checklist
docs.text:
Ask yourself weekly:

  1. Did I correct anyone publicly this week? (Don't.)
  2. Did anyone in my unit go a full week without being spoken to by name?
  3. Is my 2IC ready to run this unit without me?
  4. Who in my unit is closest to a promotion, and what specifically is holding them back?
  5. Did I ask a subordinate for honest feedback and actually listen?
  6. Did anyone leave my unit this month, and do I know why?
  7. Am I still having fun? (If no, take an LOA before you burn out and take three people with you.)

Command Handbook v1.0 — Effective [DATE] — Acknowledgment required before assuming any command position

docs.title: [SERVER NAME] — Certification Standards
docs.text: Document 6 of 6 · Version 1.0 · Authority: High Command + Instructor Corps

docs.title: 0. The System
docs.text:
Rank tells you where you sit in the chain. Qualifications tell you what you can do.

Separating these is the core progression design of this server. You do not unlock a heavy weapon by being promoted; you unlock it by proving you can use it. A Corporal with EOD can do things a Captain without it cannot.

docs.title: Universal Rules
docs.text: Rule Detail Instructor required All certification is delivered by a holder of the Instructor qualification Practical required Every qual has a hands-on component. No qual is awarded on a written test alone. Logged Certifications post to the personnel file with date, instructor, and score Revocable Negligence or misuse suspends the qual pending recertification (Command Handbook §6.2) Currency Flight and EOD require currency (see individual syllabi). Others do not expire. Retry cooldown 3 days. No lifetime bars. Feedback mandatory Pass or fail, the candidate gets specific written feedback Duration cap No qualification course exceeds 45 minutes

docs.title: Qualification Index
docs.text: # Qualification Prerequisite Difficulty 1 Basic Rifleman None Entry 2 Marksman Basic Rifleman Moderate 3 Combat Medic Basic Rifleman Moderate 4 Demolitions / EOD Basic Rifleman, CPL High 5 Heavy Weapons Basic Rifleman, 15 hrs Moderate 6 Comms / Sensor Operator Basic Rifleman Moderate 7 Armor Crew Basic Rifleman, 20 hrs Moderate 8 Flight — Starfighter Basic Rifleman, 25 hrs High 9 Flight — Transport Starfighter or 40 hrs High 10 Instructor 2 quals, SGT High

docs.title: QUAL 01 — BASIC RIFLEMAN
docs.text: Prerequisite: None — this is boot camp Duration: 25 minutes Instructor: Any Instructor-qualified NCO Unlocks: DC-15A rifle, DC-15S carbine, DC-17 pistol, deployment eligibility

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Every trooper leaves this course able to move, shoot, communicate, and report without needing to be told how.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Orientation 5 min Chain of command, ranks, courtesies, salute, reporting procedure Weapons handling 5 min Draw, holster, reload, safe direction, weapons states (Cold/Tight/Free) Movement 5 min Cover vs. concealment, bounding, stacking on a door Comms 5 min Call format, five key prowords, "man down," "contact," "check fire" Live range 5 min 10 targets at close and medium range

docs.title: Standards — must pass all
docs.text:
• Correct salute and reporting statement
  • Demonstrate all three weapons states on command
  • Correctly transmit one call in standard format
  • 6 of 10 targets on the range
  • Zero friendly-fire incidents during the course

docs.title: Failure
docs.text: Immediate retry permitted, same session. Nobody leaves boot camp unqualified. If a candidate can't pass in two attempts, the instructor works with them individually. This is the one course we do not gate.

docs.title: QUAL 02 — MARKSMAN
docs.text: Prerequisite: Basic Rifleman Duration: 30 minutes Unlocks: DC-15x sniper rifle, scoped optics, designated marksman role

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Precision fire at range with positive identification, target discrimination, and useful reporting from an overwatch position.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Fundamentals 5 min Positions, breathing, trigger control, holdover Optics 5 min Zeroing, range estimation, magnification discipline Position selection 5 min Cover, concealment, fields of fire, displacement Observation 5 min SPOTREP format from an overwatch position Qualification course 10 min Scored live-fire

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
Stage Requirement Static, long range 8/10 Moving targets 5/8 Mixed hostile/friendly discrimination 10/10 hostiles, 0 friendlies SPOTREP One correct transmission

Any friendly hit is an automatic fail. No partial credit. A marksman who cannot discriminate is more dangerous than no marksman.

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text: Two friendly-fire incidents in operations within 30 days = automatic suspension pending recert.

docs.title: QUAL 03 — COMBAT MEDIC
docs.text: Prerequisite: Basic Rifleman Duration: 35 minutes Unlocks: Bacta injectors, revive capability, triage tools, medbay post eligibility

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Treat casualties under fire without becoming one, and manage a casualty collection point.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Triage 5 min Priority order: immediate → serious → walking wounded Care under fire 10 min Suppress or break contact first, drag technique, casualty positioning Treatment 5 min Bacta application, stabilization, revive procedure CCP management 5 min Establishing and running a casualty collection point CASREP 5 min Report format and transmission Practical scenario 5 min Three casualties under fire, scored

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Correctly triage 3 casualties in priority order
  • Treat under fire without taking a casualty yourself
  • One correct CASREP transmission
  • Establish a CCP in a defensible position
  • Practical scenario: all three casualties recovered, medic survives

docs.title: Notes for Instructors
docs.text: Emphasize the discipline that saves medics: the area gets secured first, every time. A medic who runs into open fire is a second casualty and a squad without medical support. Teach them to say "suppress that window" before they move.

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text: Repeated abandonment of casualties in operations, or persistent failure to secure before treating.

docs.title: QUAL 04 — DEMOLITIONS / EOD
docs.text: Prerequisite: Basic Rifleman, rank of Corporal Duration: 40 minutes Unlocks: Thermal detonators, breaching charges, mine clearing tools, demolition role Currency: Requires one refresher every 90 days

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Employ explosives safely in proximity to friendly forces, and render safe emplaced devices.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Safety 10 min Minimum safe distance, danger close, "frag out," blast radius awareness Breaching 10 min Charge placement on doors and walls, stack positioning, initiation sequence Demolition 5 min Objective destruction, timing, sequencing EOD 10 min Identification, cordon, render safe procedure Practical 5 min Scored breach and render-safe

docs.title: Standards
docs.text: Requirement Threshold Safety brief before every charge 100% "Frag out" called before every throw 100% Friendly casualties from your ordnance Zero — automatic fail Successful breach 3/3 Render safe 2/2

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text: One friendly casualty from your ordnance in an operation suspends this qualification immediately, pending investigation and full recertification. This is the strictest revocation standard on the server, and deliberately so.

docs.title: QUAL 05 — HEAVY WEAPONS
docs.text: Prerequisite: Basic Rifleman, 15 hours duty time Duration: 30 minutes Unlocks: Z-6 rotary cannon, RPS-6 launcher, heavy gunner role

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Deliver and sustain suppressive fire, and employ anti-armor weapons without endangering friendlies.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Suppression theory 5 min What suppression is for, sustained vs. cyclic rates Position 5 min Emplacement, fields of fire, cover, displacement timing Anti-armor 10 min Backblast area, target selection, engagement ranges Coordination 5 min Working with maneuver elements, lifting and shifting fire Practical 5 min Scored suppression and anti-armor engagement

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Sustain suppression on a position for 30 seconds without overheating
  • Lift fire correctly on command as friendlies advance
  • Destroy 2/2 armor targets
  • Backblast area clear on every launch — a friendly in backblast is an automatic fail
  • Displace after firing from a fixed position

docs.title: Notes for Instructors
docs.text: The common failure is treating the Z-6 as a big rifle. Teach that suppression is a support function — the gunner's job is to make the enemy keep their heads down so someone else can move. Score coordination, not kills.

docs.title: QUAL 06 — COMMS / SENSOR OPERATOR
docs.text: Prerequisite: Basic Rifleman Duration: 30 minutes Unlocks: Long-range comms equipment, sensor console, campaign map access, bridge post eligibility

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Run a net cleanly, relay accurately, and translate sensor data into usable information for command.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Net structure 5 min Command / battalion / squad / emergency nets, when to use each Procedure 10 min Full proword and brevity set, priority traffic, net discipline calls Reports 5 min SITREP, SPOTREP, CASREP formats — writing and receiving Sensors 5 min Contact classification, plotting, reporting to command Practical 5 min Run a net during a scripted multi-element scenario

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• 100% correct proword usage during the practical
  • Correctly receive, record, and relay three reports without error
  • Correctly prioritize when two elements transmit simultaneously
  • Call "ALL STATIONS, NET DISCIPLINE" appropriately when the net degrades
  • Plot and report three sensor contacts accurately

docs.title: Notes for Instructors
docs.text: This is the most undervalued qualification on the server and one of the most important. A good comms operator makes a mediocre operation feel professional. Recruit deliberately for it — the people who are good at it are often not the people who volunteer.

docs.title: QUAL 07 — ARMOR CREW
docs.text: Prerequisite: Basic Rifleman, 20 hours duty time Duration: 35 minutes Unlocks: AT-RT operation, AT-TE crew positions, BARC speeder

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Operate ground vehicles in coordination with dismounted infantry, without running them over.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Familiarization 5 min Controls, crew positions, capabilities and limits Driving 10 min Terrain handling, obstacle negotiation, hull-down positioning Gunnery 10 min Target engagement, traverse, coordination with the driver Infantry coordination 5 min Tank-infantry comms, dismount safety, sector responsibility Practical 5 min Scored course with dismounts present

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Complete the driving course without disabling the vehicle
  • 6/8 gunnery targets
  • Zero friendly casualties from movement or fire — automatic fail
  • Maintain comms with a dismounted element throughout
  • Correctly execute a hull-down position

docs.title: Notes for Instructors
docs.text: The dominant failure mode is armor outrunning its infantry and dying alone. Score the practical on whether the dismounts survived, not on how fast the vehicle finished.

docs.title: QUAL 08 — FLIGHT: STARFIGHTER
docs.text: Prerequisite: Basic Rifleman, 25 hours duty time Duration: 45 minutes (may be split across two sessions) Unlocks: ARC-170, V-19 Torrent Currency: 3 sim deck flight hours per 30 days, or qualification goes inactive

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Launch, navigate, engage, and recover a starfighter without losing the airframe.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Ground school 10 min Airframe, controls, flight envelope, hangar procedure Launch & recovery 10 min Launch sequence, pattern, approach, landing — the hard part Navigation 5 min Waypoints, formation flying, wingman position Combat maneuvering 10 min Engagement geometry, defensive maneuvers, gun employment Check ride 10 min Full profile, scored by a qualified instructor pilot

docs.title: Check Ride Standards
docs.text:
Stage Requirement Launch Correct sequence, comms with deck Formation Hold wingman position for 60 seconds Engagement 3/5 targets destroyed Defensive Survive 60 seconds against an instructor Recovery Land intact — automatic fail if the airframe is lost

Landing is the qualification. Anyone can fly. Bringing it home is the skill, and it's what separates a pilot from a very expensive one-time asset.

docs.title: Prerequisites Note
docs.text: Sim deck flight hours count toward the 25-hour requirement. Encourage candidates to log sim time before attempting the check ride — a first-attempt failure is common and shouldn't discourage anyone.

docs.title: QUAL 09 — FLIGHT: TRANSPORT
docs.text: Prerequisite: Starfighter qualification, or 40 hours duty time Duration: 45 minutes Unlocks: LAAT/i gunship, troop insertion and extraction role Currency: 3 sim deck flight hours per 30 days

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Insert and extract troops under fire, on time, at the right coordinates, without killing your passengers.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Airframe 5 min LAAT capabilities, load limits, door gunner coordination Insertion 15 min LZ selection, approach under fire, hot vs. cold LZ procedure Extraction 10 min Emergency extraction, casualty loading, "popsicle" response Coordination 10 min Working with the ground element, timing, comms Check ride 5 min Full insert-extract profile with live passengers

docs.title: Check Ride Standards
docs.text:
• Insert 6 passengers at the correct LZ within 60 seconds of the briefed time
  • Zero passenger casualties on insertion or extraction
  • Execute a hot-LZ extraction under fire
  • Maintain comms with the ground element throughout
  • Return the airframe intact

docs.title: Notes for Instructors
docs.text: Transport pilots have the least glory and the most responsibility on the server — everyone else's operation depends on them being where they said they'd be, when they said they'd be there. Recognize them accordingly. A reliable LAAT pilot is worth three fighter aces.

docs.title: QUAL 10 — INSTRUCTOR
docs.text: Prerequisite: Two qualifications held, rank of Sergeant, officer nomination Duration: 45 minutes Unlocks: Authority to certify others in qualifications you personally hold

docs.title: Why This Is the Keystone
docs.text:
This qualification is the one that lets the server survive its own growth.

Once players can certify other players, the training pipeline stops depending on staff availability. A server where only three people can run courses is a server with a three-person bottleneck on all progression. Build the instructor corps early and aggressively.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Deliver a qualification course to standard, assess fairly against a published rubric, and give feedback a person can actually act on.

docs.title: Course Outline
docs.text: Block Time Content Instructional method 10 min Explain → demonstrate → practice → assess. Why lecture alone fails. Rubric discipline 5 min Scoring to the published standard, not to your personal preference Feedback delivery 10 min Specific, behavioral, actionable. "Your muzzle drifted left on the reload" not "be better." Failure handling 5 min Delivering a fail without discouraging a retry Prohibited practices 5 min No hazing. No endurance filtering. No hard time gates. No favoritism. Practical: teach a block 10 min Candidate teaches a 10-minute segment to a live class, scored

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Deliver the practical block using all four instructional phases
  • Score three sample candidates against a rubric within one point of the assessor
  • Deliver one pass and one fail with specific, actionable feedback
  • Correctly identify prohibited practices in three scenario examples
  • Class engagement: did the students actually learn it? Assessed by asking them.

docs.title: Instructor Code
docs.text:
1. You are not the point. The student is.
  2. Teach the standard, score the standard, nothing else.
  3. Never fail someone without telling them exactly how to pass.
  4. No hazing, ever, in any form, for any reason.
  5. Keep it under the time limit. Every time you run long, you make the next class smaller.
  6. If everyone fails, the course is broken — not the students.
  7. Recognize the student who improves most, not just the one who scores highest.

docs.title: Ongoing Requirement
docs.text:
• Deliver minimum one course per month to remain current
  • Instructor performance is reviewed by student feedback, collected anonymously
  • Poor instructor feedback is a coaching item first, a suspension second

docs.title: Appendix A — Certification Log Format
docs.text:
Every certification records:

Candidate designation · Qualification · Date · Instructor · Score by block · Pass/Defer/Fail · Written feedback · Recertification due (if applicable)

Logs post to the personnel file and are visible to the candidate, their chain of command, and promotion boards.

docs.title: Appendix B — Suspension and Recertification
docs.text:
Trigger Result Negligence causing friendly casualty Immediate suspension, full recert required Currency lapse (flight, EOD) Inactive status, refresher required Pattern of misuse Suspension, command review Charter violation involving the qualified capability Suspension pending staff resolution

Recertification is the full course, not a shortened version. The qualification means the same thing whether it's your first or your third.

docs.title: Appendix C — Build Priority
docs.text:
If you're standing up the instructor corps from nothing, certify in this order:

  1. Basic Rifleman instructors — you need volume immediately
  2. Instructor qualification itself — build the multiplier early
  3. Combat Medic — highest impact on operation quality
  4. Comms — makes everything else feel professional
  5. Marksman, Heavy Weapons — high demand, easy to teach
  6. Flight — high effort, gate behind sim deck hours
  7. EOD, Armor — specialist, lower volume

Qualification Syllabi v1.0 — Effective [DATE] — Rubrics maintained separately by the Instructor Corps

docs.title: [SERVER NAME] — Grand Army of the Republic
docs.text: Document 3 of 6 · Version 1.0 · Authority: High Command

docs.title: 0. How To Use This Document
docs.text:
This is the practical manual. Formations, comms, engagement, casualties, posts. It is written to be learnable in one sitting and referenced in ten seconds.

Section 3 (Communications) is the single highest-value page in this entire document set. If a new trooper reads exactly one thing, make it that.

Standard of enforcement: teach once, correct once, enforce on the third. Nobody gets punished for a procedure nobody taught them.

docs.title: 1.1 When Bearing Is Required
docs.text:
In effect: formations, briefings, operations, training, at posts, in the presence of an officer, on the bridge, in the brig.

Not in effect: barracks, mess, sim deck between runs, off-duty hours, Discord social channels.

The barracks should be loud. That is not a failure of discipline — it is the actual thing we are recreating. Discipline is knowing which room you're in.

docs.title: 1.2 Courtesies
docs.text:
• "Sir" / "Ma'am" to commissioned officers (2LT and above). Non-commissioned officers are addressed by rank: "Sergeant," "Corporal."
  • Salute on first meeting an officer each session, on reporting, on being dismissed. Not required in a combat zone, in the field, or when your hands are full.
  • Stand at attention when an officer of Captain or above enters a formation.
  • Reporting: "Sir, CT-2247 reporting as ordered."
  • Acknowledgment: "Yes, sir," "Understood," "Copy," "Wilco." Not "ok," "sure," "yeah."

docs.title: 1.3 Positions
docs.text: Command Position Attention Feet together, arms at sides, eyes forward, no movement, no talking Parade Rest Feet apart, hands behind back, eyes forward, no talking At Ease May move and speak quietly, one foot remains planted Fall Out Formation dismissed

docs.title: 2.1 The Ten-Minute Rule
docs.text:
A formation runs ten minutes. Fifteen is the hard ceiling.

A formation that runs long is a leadership failure and will be treated as one. If you cannot deliver it in ten minutes, you are giving a briefing instead — call it that, let people sit, and stop making them stand at attention through it.

Nothing kills a server faster than the forty-five-minute formation.

docs.title: 2.2 Formation Types
docs.text: Type Purpose Duration Frequency Roll Call Accountability, quick assignments 5 min Start of session Battalion Formation Unit-level announcements, promotions 10 min Weekly Operation Formation Pre-op assembly, immediately precedes briefing 5 min Before each op Ceremonial Promotions, awards, memorials 15 min As required Emergency Muster Base alert, boarding, immediate response 2 min As required

docs.title: 2.3 Standard Sequence
docs.text:
1. Call — "[UNIT], FALL IN" over comms and in chat
  2. Assembly — 60 seconds to arrive; latecomers fall in at the rear without disruption
  3. Attention — "[UNIT], ATTENTION"
  4. Accountability — count off or roll call
  5. Business — announcements, promotions, assignments. This is the ten-minute window.
  6. Questions — "Any questions?" and mean it
  7. Dismissal — "[UNIT], FALL OUT"

docs.title: 2.4 Formation Discipline
docs.text:
• Arrive on time. Late without notice is a counseling item after the second occurrence.
  • No talking at attention. Questions go at the end.
  • No leaving formation without permission.
  • If you must go AFK, say so in OOC chat before the formation starts.
  • Leadership does not use formations for punishment. Mass corrective action for one person's mistake is banned. It builds resentment and it drives people off the server.

docs.title: 3. Communications
docs.text: This is the section that matters most. Learn it.

docs.title: 3.1 Net Structure
docs.text:
Net Users Purpose Command Net Officers, battalion leads, Naval Coordination between units Battalion Net All members of a battalion Unit-level traffic Squad Net 3–6 troopers Fire team traffic Emergency Net All Life-safety only Local Voice Proximity Everything not requiring radio

Use the lowest net that solves the problem. Squad chatter does not go on Command Net.

docs.title: 3.2 Callsign Format
docs.text:
[UNIT] [ELEMENT] [POSITION] — spoken as: "Wolf Two-One" = Wolfpack, 2nd squad, position 1 (squad lead).

Command elements use the unit name plus "Actual": "Wolf Actual" is the Wolfpack commander.

docs.title: 3.3 Standard Call Format
docs.text:
"[WHO YOU'RE CALLING], THIS IS [WHO YOU ARE], [MESSAGE], OVER."

Example: "Wolf Actual, this is Wolf Two-One, we're taking fire from the north ridge, requesting support, over."

After contact is established, shorten: "Two-One, moving."

docs.title: 3.4 Prowords
docs.text: Proword Meaning Over I'm done, respond Out I'm done, no response needed Roger I received and understood Wilco Received, understood, and I will comply Say again Repeat your last (never say "repeat") Standby Wait, I'm busy Break Separating parts of a long message Correction I made an error, here's the fix How copy Did you receive that? Negative / Affirmative No / yes Interrogative I'm asking a question

docs.title: 3.5 Brevity Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning Contact Enemy sighted Engaging I am firing Troops in contact Under fire, need support Man down Casualty, unspecified Man down, [callsign] Named casualty Bacta / Medic Medical assistance required Moving Advancing Set In position Clear Area cleared of threats Frag out Throwing a detonator Reloading Cover me Check fire Stop firing immediately Danger close Friendlies near target Falling back Withdrawing Winchester Out of ammunition Popsicle Emergency extraction required

docs.title: 3.6 Discipline Rules
docs.text:
1. Think before you key. Compose the message, then transmit.
  2. Brevity is a duty. Every second you hold the net, someone else can't report a casualty.
  3. Do not step on transmissions. Wait for "over" or "out."
  4. Priority: emergency > command > tactical > everything else. "Check fire" and "man down" interrupt anything.
  5. No chatter on operation nets. Save it for local voice or squad.
  6. Push to talk. Always.
  7. If comms discipline collapses, the ranking element calls "ALL STATIONS, NET DISCIPLINE" and traffic stops until reset.

docs.title: 3.7 Report Formats
docs.text:
SITREP — Situation Report, on request or every 10 minutes during an op:

Callsign · Location · Status (green/amber/red) · Enemy contact · Ammunition · Casualties · Intentions

SPOTREP — Enemy sighted:

Callsign · Size · Activity · Location · Time · Equipment

CASREP — Casualty:

Callsign · Location · Number of casualties · Severity · Extraction required Y/N

docs.title: 4.1 Standing ROE
docs.text:
1. Positive identification before engaging. Confirm target is hostile.
  2. Fire discipline. Aimed fire. No spray. No shooting through friendlies.
  3. Check your background. Know what's behind your target.
  4. Cease fire immediately on "check fire." No exceptions, no "one more shot."
  5. Friendly fire is reportable. Once is an accident. Twice in a session is a counseling item. A pattern is a qualification suspension.
  6. Surrendered enemies are prisoners. Droids may be disabled; organic surrenders are taken into custody.
  7. Non-combatants are not targets. Civilians in event scenarios are protected. Engaging them is a serious ROE violation.
  8. Do not engage outside your assigned sector without notifying adjacent elements.

docs.title: 4.2 Weapons States
docs.text:
State Meaning Weapons Cold Holstered. Base default outside alert conditions. Weapons Tight Drawn, fire only on positive ID and threat Weapons Free Fire on identified hostiles at discretion

Weapons state is set by the ranking element and announced. Base default is Weapons Cold. Running around the Venator with a rifle out is a fail-RP item.

docs.title: 4.3 Alert Conditions
docs.text: Condition Meaning Response Condition Green Normal operations Standard posts Condition Amber Elevated threat All hands to posts, weapons tight Condition Red Under attack / boarding Emergency muster, weapons free in contested compartments Condition Black Catastrophic — hull breach, abandon Evacuation protocol

docs.title: 5.1 Post Standards
docs.text:
• Report on time and in uniform. Relieving trooper receives a brief handover: status, anything unusual, standing orders.
  • A post is not an AFK spot. Duty credit accrues from presence and activity. Standing motionless for 20 minutes stops accrual.
  • Do not leave a post unrelieved. If you must go, notify your chain and get a relief.

docs.title: 5.2 Standard Posts
docs.text: Post Held by Duties Hangar Deck Any battalion Craft servicing, launch/recovery, deck safety Armory Any battalion Issue and return of equipment, inventory logging Brig Coruscant Guard Prisoner supervision, intake, release Main Gate / Airlock Coruscant Guard ID verification, access control Bridge Naval Sensors, navigation, comms, campaign map Medbay Medics Triage, treatment, records Roving Patrol Any battalion Sweep route, report anomalies

docs.title: 5.3 Handover Brief
docs.text: "Post is [status]. Standing orders are [X]. During my watch, [events]. Nothing further." / "Post is green, nothing to report."

docs.title: 6. Casualty Procedures
docs.text:
1. Call it. "Man down, [callsign], [location]" on the appropriate net.
  2. Secure the area first. Do not create a second casualty. Suppress or break contact before treating.
  3. Casualty collection point. Move casualties to a designated CCP rather than treating in the open.
  4. Medic priority order: immediate life threats → serious → walking wounded.
  5. KIA handling: in operations, remain down until medic or extraction reaches you, or until the New Life Rule timer expires. Do not immediately respawn and sprint back into the fight — it destroys the tension and makes medics pointless.
  6. After-action: casualties are logged in the operation AAR.

Medic protection is everyone's job. A squad that lets its medic get shot has failed.

docs.title: 7. Prisoner Handling
docs.text:
1. Search on capture. Remove weapons and equipment.
  2. Silence and segregate — prisoners do not talk to each other during transport.
  3. Speed — move to the brig promptly.
  4. Safeguard — prisoners are not to be harmed, mocked, or used as roleplay props. Abuse of a prisoner is a Charter violation, not just fail-RP.
  5. Tag — log the capture: who, where, when, by whom.
  6. Custody passes to the Coruscant Guard at the brig. They own the prisoner from that point.
  7. Interrogation requires an officer present and follows the Command Handbook. No torture roleplay.

docs.title: 8.1 The Five-Paragraph Order
docs.text:
Every operation briefing follows this structure. It takes five minutes and it makes the difference between a coordinated op and forty people wandering.

  1. Situation — what's happening, enemy, friendly forces
  2. Mission — one sentence: who, what, when, where, why
  3. Execution — commander's intent, scheme of maneuver, tasks per element
  4. Sustainment — ammunition, medical, extraction plan
  5. Command & Signal — chain of command, net assignments, callsigns

docs.title: 8.2 Operation Flow
docs.text: Phase Content Muster Formation, accountability, weapons/kit check Brief Five-paragraph order, questions Insert Movement to objective Actions on objective The mission Extract Withdrawal, accountability check Debrief / AAR Ten minutes maximum, see §8.3

docs.title: 8.3 After Action Review
docs.text:
Four questions, ten minutes, everyone participates:

  1. What was supposed to happen?
  2. What actually happened?
  3. What went well?
  4. What do we change next time?

AAR rules: no rank in the AAR — a CT may tell a Colonel the plan was bad. No blaming individuals. Findings go in the operation log and feed the campaign map.

An AAR where nobody criticizes anything is a wasted AAR.

docs.title: 9. Uniform and Kit Standards
docs.text:
• Phase II armor is standard. Unit markings correct for your battalion.
  • Kit must match your qualifications. Carrying a DC-15x without Marksman qual is a fail-RP item and an armory violation.
  • Naval personnel wear the naval uniform, not armor, except during boarding actions.
  • Helmets on in operations, at exterior posts, and during alert conditions. Helmets optional in barracks, mess, and medbay.
  • Cosmetic customization must remain within the Canon Scope. No armor from outside the era.

docs.title: 10. Quick Reference Card
docs.text:
Formation: 10 minutes. Attention = silent. Questions at the end. Radio: "[Them], this is [Me], [message], over." Priority traffic: Check fire. Man down. Contact. Base default: Weapons Cold, Condition Green. Casualty: Call it → secure area → CCP → treat. Reporting: "Sir, [designation] reporting as ordered." When corrected: "Copy" or "Wilco." Move on.

docs.title: [SERVER NAME] — Out-of-Character Authority
docs.text: Document 4 of 6 · Version 1.0 · Authority: Head of Staff + Management

docs.title: 0. The Job
docs.text:
Staff exist for exactly three purposes:

  1. Keep players safe from harassment, hate, and predatory behavior
  2. Keep the game fair — no cheating, no exploiting, no griefing
  3. Keep the server running — technical issues, stuck players, broken props

That's it. Staff do not run the roleplay, do not resolve in-character disputes, do not command troops, and do not use their tools to shape the story.

If you took this position for the powers, you took it for the wrong reason and it will show within a month.

docs.title: 1. The Firewall
docs.text:
This is the most important rule in this handbook. Read it twice.

Staff authority grants zero in-character authority. Command authority grants zero staff powers.

Staff Rank Command Rank Handles Rules, cheating, harassment, tech Promotions, tryouts, IC discipline, operations Grants Ban, kick, mute, noclip, spawn Orders, promotion authority, IC punishment Does NOT grant Any in-character standing whatsoever Any moderation tool or authority

In practice: - A Superadmin playing a CT takes orders from a Sergeant and says "Yes, Sergeant." - A Marshal Commander cannot ban, kick, mute, or issue a warning. - You may hold both. If you do, you declare which hat you're wearing the moment it matters: "Stepping out of character as staff for a second." - You may never use staff tools in a dispute you are personally party to in character. Call another staff member. Every time. No exceptions.

Violating the firewall is the fastest way off the staff team. It is a Strike-and-review offense on the first occurrence.

docs.title: 2. Rank Structure and Powers
docs.text:
Rank Tenure Powers Trial Moderator 2 weeks Kick, mute (≤24h), warn, teleport-to, noclip in sits, freeze Moderator — + Ban (≤3 days), bring/return, spectate, gag Administrator — + Ban (≤14 days), jail, model/job change, review Moderator actions Senior Administrator — + Ban (≤30 days), handle appeals, approve tier adjustments >1, mentor Trials Head of Staff 6mo term + Permanent ban, promote/demote to Administrator, final appeal authority Management — + All server access, promote/demote Head of Staff, policy authority

Powers are ceilings, not targets. Use the least force that solves the problem. A conversation solves more sits than a ban does.

docs.title: 3.1 Application
docs.text:
• Minimum 2 weeks and 20 hours on the server
  • Age 16+ (18+ for Senior Administrator and above)
  • Clean record for 60 days
  • Written application + voice interview
  • We hire for temperament, not activity hours. The calmest person in a bad situation is the person we want.

docs.title: 3.2 Trial Period
docs.text:
Two weeks. Trial Moderators are shadowed — a Moderator or above reviews their sits.

  • Weekly check-in with an assigned mentor
  • All sits logged and reviewed
  • Roughly one in three trials should not pass. This is normal and expected. Failing a trial is not a black mark and does not bar reapplication after 60 days.

Pass criteria: correct rule application, calm demeanor under pressure, evidence discipline, asked for help when unsure. That last one is weighted heavily — a Trial who escalates appropriately is worth more than one who guesses confidently.

docs.title: 3.3 Activity
docs.text:
• Minimum 6 hours/week on staff duty
  • Respond to reports within a session
  • Leave of Absence is free and unlimited — post it in the staff channel and go. LOA does not count against activity, does not affect standing, and does not require justification.

Burnout kills staff teams. Take the LOA.

docs.title: 3.4 Term Limits
docs.text:
• Head of Staff: 6-month terms, renewable once by Management review, then a mandatory 3-month step-down.
  • Term limits exist so leadership can rotate without anyone having to quit angrily. Stepping down at term end is an honorable exit, not a demotion.

docs.title: 4. Evidence Standards
docs.text:
The single hardest rule on this server:

No evidence, no punishment. If a punishment log has no evidence attached, the appeal is granted automatically.

There is no exception to this. Not for obvious cases. Not for repeat offenders. Not for Management.

docs.title: 4.1 What Counts
docs.text: Offense type Required evidence Chat violation Screenshot with timestamp and surrounding context, or log excerpt Voice violation Audio clip, or 2+ independent witness statements Cheating Video clip, minimum 30 seconds, showing the behavior Exploiting Video clip showing the exploit being used RDM / griefing Video clip or damage logs plus witness statement Prop abuse Screenshot plus prop ownership log Harassment Screenshots of the pattern, not a single message

docs.title: 4.2 Standards
docs.text:
• Context is mandatory. A screenshot of one line without what preceded it is not evidence, it's a fragment.
  • Clips must show the behavior, not the aftermath.
  • Witness statements are collected separately. Do not let witnesses discuss it first.
  • "I saw it happen" from the reporting staff member is evidence, but it must be written into the log as a statement with detail, not asserted as fact.
  • Evidence is attached to the log at the time of punishment, not gathered later if challenged.
  • Retention: 12 months.

docs.title: 4.3 Burden
docs.text: The burden is on us, always. Uncertain means no punishment. A warning you're unsure about does more damage to the community than a violation you let slide — because the violation affects one incident, and an unjust warning affects that player's entire relationship with the server.

docs.title: 5.1 Procedure
docs.text:
1. Acknowledge the report — "On my way" or "Standby, in another sit." Never leave a report unacknowledged.
  2. Gather evidence before pulling anyone. Check logs, spectate if needed. Do not tip off a suspected cheater by teleporting them.
  3. Pull both parties to a sit location. Reporter and reported.
  4. Let the reporter speak first, uninterrupted.
  5. Let the reported speak, uninterrupted.
  6. Ask clarifying questions. Do not lecture.
  7. Rule. State the rule, the finding, and the punishment plainly.
  8. Log it — rule, evidence, punishment, reasoning.
  9. Return both parties.

docs.title: 5.2 Conduct in a Sit
docs.text:
Do: - Stay calm regardless of how you're spoken to - Explain the rule, not just the punishment - Tell them how to appeal - Thank the reporter, even if the report didn't hold up

Don't: - Argue. State and move on. - Threaten additional punishment for arguing. - Discuss other players' punishments. - Make jokes at anyone's expense. - Rule on something you're not sure about — escalate instead.

docs.title: 5.3 When You're Being Abused
docs.text:
You are not required to absorb abuse. If a player becomes hostile:

  1. Warn once: "I'm ending this sit if this continues."
  2. If it continues, end the sit, issue the appropriate punishment for the conduct, and return them.
  3. Log it and move on.

You do not have to win the argument. You are not required to make them agree with you.

docs.title: 6. Escalation
docs.text:
Escalate — do not guess — when:

  • The punishment would exceed your ban limit
  • The case involves another staff member
  • The case involves Management or Head of Staff
  • You are personally involved in the incident
  • Cheating is suspected but evidence is ambiguous
  • It's a Tier 4 or 5 offense
  • The rule is unclear or the situation isn't covered
  • You are angry

That last one is real. If you are angry, hand it off. There is no shame in "I'm too heated for this one, can someone take it."

Escalation path: Trial → Moderator → Administrator → Senior Administrator → Head of Staff → Ombudsman (for cases involving the chain itself) → Management.

docs.title: 7. Conflict of Interest
docs.text:
You must recuse yourself and call another staff member when:

  • You are a party to the incident, in or out of character
  • The player is in your battalion and the issue is battalion-related
  • The player is a close friend or someone you have ongoing conflict with
  • You issued the original punishment being appealed
  • You stand to gain in character from the outcome

Recusal is free and expected. Nobody thinks less of you for it. The cost of not recusing is that every ruling you ever make becomes suspect.

docs.title: 8. Staff Conduct Rules
docs.text: # Rule 8.1 Do not use staff tools for personal gain, entertainment, or in-character advantage. 8.2 Do not spawn items, weapons, or props for yourself or others outside of approved events. 8.3 Do not noclip, godmode, or spectate outside of an active sit or approved event duty. 8.4 Do not discuss active cases, punishments, or appeals outside the staff channel. 8.5 Do not accept anything of value from a player in connection with your duties. 8.6 Do not use staff status to obtain in-character rank, qualifications, or roles. 8.7 Do not give donors preferential treatment. Donation status is invisible in a sit. 8.8 Do not retaliate against a player who appealed your ruling or reported you. 8.9 Do not leak internal staff discussion. 8.10 Hold yourself to the Charter more strictly than anyone else, publicly.

docs.title: Two-Strike Policy
docs.text:
Strike One: Documented in the staff record. Made known to the staff team — not to the public, but not hidden from peers either. Corrective conversation with Head of Staff.

Strike Two: Removal from the staff team.

Immediate removal, no strikes, for: - Firewall violation (using staff tools in a personal IC dispute) - Punishing without evidence, twice - Retaliation against a reporter or appellant - Falsifying evidence or logs - Any Charter Tier 4 or 5 violation - Preferential treatment for payment

Strikes expire after 6 months of clean conduct.

Removed staff may reapply after 90 days, except where removal was for falsified evidence or retaliation, which are permanent bars.

docs.title: Right of Appeal
docs.text: Staff have the same appeal rights as players. A removed staff member may appeal to the Ombudsman, who may escalate to the Owner.

docs.title: 10. The Ombudsman
docs.text:
Appointed by Management, 6-month term, explicitly outside the staff and command chains.

  • Receives complaints about anyone, including Head of Staff and Management
  • Has standing to escalate directly to the Owner
  • Cannot issue punishments — the role is investigative and advisory only
  • Publishes an anonymized quarterly summary: complaint volume, categories, resolution rate

Why this exists: every community that collapses does so because grievances had nowhere to go except a public Discord blowup. This is the pressure release valve. It costs nothing and it has saved communities.

docs.title: 11. Shift Coverage
docs.text:
• Peak hours (7–11pm local) require minimum 2 staff online.
  • Post your availability in the staff channel weekly.
  • The staff channel is for staff business. Social chat belongs elsewhere — a staff channel that becomes a clique lounge is the beginning of the end.
  • Weekly staff meeting, 30 minutes, agenda published in advance, notes posted after.

docs.title: 12. The Standard
docs.text:
Every staff decision gets measured against one question:

Would this decision look defensible if it were posted publicly, with full context, tomorrow?

If yes, act. If no, don't. If you're not sure, escalate.

That's the whole job.
